correctness.rationale: The unordered two-particle discrete configuration complex is reconstructed from the 12-vertex, 24-edge cuboctahedral graph. The bundled verifier checks all 66 zero-cells, 240 one-cells and 204 two-cells, the signed chain identity, a connected one-skeleton, a determinant-1 rank-161 minor of the two-boundary after integral spanning-tree cycle coordinates, and 43 independent integral two-cycles with a unimodular coordinate block. These certificates force torsion-free H_1 of rank 14 and free H_2 of rank 43. The same reconstruction checks the signed action of all 48 graph automorphisms and recomputes every rational character value and irreducible multiplicity. The only topological input beyond the finite chain computation is the standard sufficient-subdivision theorem; for two particles its path and loop bounds are satisfied because the graph is simple and has girth 3.

value.rationale: The cuboctahedral graph is a canonical highly symmetric Archimedean graph, and automorphism actions on graph-configuration homology are part of the natural functorial structure emphasized by the owning literature. The result gives the complete rational symmetry module in every positive homological degree, refining planar Betti data into ten class traces and irreducible multiplicities. This is structurally informative rather than a parameter-only recomputation: for example the central orientation-reversing symmetry has trace 0 on \(H_1\) but -7 on \(H_2\), and the two central sectors have different \(S_4\) content. The exact finite certificate makes the graph-specific refinement reusable for equivariant comparisons.
